output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses most likely comes from the 12 August relay server move. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules, including the 15-second hold-off, repeat-notification suppression and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone. The IT team's test and sign-off didn't catch it. Since then, phone notifications per nurse in Pods A-C have roughly doubled (about 38 to 80+ per shift). Acknowledgement time doubled, from 34 to 71 seconds. Incidents rose about fivefold for core, agency and new-graduate nurses alike. Pod D, still on the old server, saw no change, even though its agency share is similar. That rules out agency staffing, acuity and the monitor update as main causes. Bedside alarm volume was flat, and there was no step on 23-24 September. Sick leave rising with the alarm load is plausible but not proven. I'm fairly confident (about 85-90%). Don't cap agency use or open performance reviews. That would punish the wrong people. Don't switch off SpO2 phone forwarding either. Instead, restore the rules (about 4 hours plus clinical validation), get Clinical Engineering and the alarm committee to sign off, and track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Check the room 14 reports of phones not ringing separately. Wireless coverage is unconfirmed.
